standard_prerequisites: A universe type and the identity type of the universe between two of its elements.
The identity function on the universe regarded as a type family indexed by the universe, and transport along a path in a type family.
Path induction with its conversion rule.
The example that the identity function of a type is an equivalence, with its quasi-inverse structure.
core_obligations: Define the canonical function carrying an identification of types to an equivalence, by sending a path to its transport function together with the proof that the transport is an equivalence.
Prove that the transport along a path in the universe family is an equivalence.
proof_roadmap: Regard the identity function on the universe as a type family indexed by the universe, so a path between types gives a transport function from the first type to the second.
Prove the transport function is an equivalence: by path induction assume the path is reflexivity, where the transport is definitionally the identity function, an equivalence by the author's example.
Define the canonical function on a path to be its transport equipped with that equivalence proof.
difficulty_reason: One induction reducing the equivalence claim to the identity-function case; the care point is assembling the transport together with its equivalence proof into the defined function.
